title: Hybrid INT8/FP8 KV cache quantization profiles and calibration pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: develop a reproducible calibration pipeline and a set of hybrid quantization profiles for KV cache tensors that balance latency/memory gains with minimal quality regression. We will compare symmetric INT8 (per-channel) and FP8 (e4m3-like) encodings, then iterate a hybrid layout that places the more dynamic components of KV in a higher-precision format. Deliverables: 1) calibration tool that emits per-layer profiles, 2) canonical profile set for LLaMA-2-13B and MPT-7B sequence buckets, 3) automated CI regression checks and canary rollout config.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration tool produces deterministic per-layer scale/zero params from a representative corpus
Hybrid profile meets <=1.0% quality regression vs FP16 baseline (measured by normalized logprob on eval prompts) for target models
Latency improvement >=20% on 4xA100 serving config for common sequence-length buckets (<=1024 tokens)
Profiles are stored in model catalog and selectable by the router; canary rollout tests exist in console
comments: 2025-02-05 - Kickoff: scoped experiments and selected initial model targets: LLaMA-2-13B, MPT-7B. Representative calibration corpus: 10k diverse prompts (conversational + code + docs). - Aisha

2025-02-10 - Data collection: instrumentation added to runtime to stream KV activations for a small population of warm-up requests; saved 25M keys/values across buckets. See GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 - Marco

2025-02-14 - Preliminary calibration: computed per-channel symmetric INT8 scales using 99.9th percentile clipping and per-layer biased MSE minimization. Observed heavy tail in some attention heads; moved those heads into FP8 in hybrid config which reduced token-level KL divergence. Benchmark run: int8-only reduced KV memory by ~42% and kernel time by ~30% vs fp16 on 4xA100. - Marco

2025-02-18 - Quality checks: ran 2k eval prompts comparing fp16 -> int8 -> fp8 -> hybrid. Metrics: normalized logprob delta and answer-similarity. Results: int8-only: mean delta +1.6% (worse), fp8-only: +0.9%, hybrid (int8 keys + fp8 values for top-N heads): +0.6% with 28% latency reduction. Confidence intervals still wide; need more runs. - Aisha

2025-02-21 - Review feedback from ML research: suggested per-channel bias correction and small loss-scale post-compensation for heads with high drift. Added a prototype bias-correction hook in calibration pipeline. Also flagged need for sequence-length-aware profiles. - Review by Lina Torres

2025-02-23 - Integration test: added profile selector to model catalog and ran canary on dedicated pool (canary-tag: kv-quant-hybrid-2025-02). No SLO violations in 24h window. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv-quant/kv-hybrid-canary - Marco

notes: Calibration approach: collect KV activations across representative requests; compute per-channel min/max and MSE/KL objectives to choose scale. Prefer MSE for head-level fidelity and KL for distributional similarity.
Quant schemes: INT8 uses per-channel symmetric quant with clip percentile tuning. FP8 emulation uses e4m3 dynamic exponent range; we emulate on CPU with high-precision accumulation for validation.

Hybrid heuristic: identify heads with >2.5x variance vs layer median; keep those heads in FP8 (or FP16 fallback) and quantize remaining KV to INT8. This reduces catastrophic degradation from heavy-tailed heads.

Calibration cadence: profiles generated per model + seq_len_bucket (<=128, 129-512, 513-1024, >1024) and stored with timestamp/commit. Rollout config supports automatic fallback to fp16 when drift or eval regression detected.
Operational guardrails: require regression test pass on 3 eval slices (conversational, code, docs) before promoting profile to 'stable'. Canary runs must be >=24h and show no SLO violation.
Implementation note: kernel changes required to support combined int8 keys + float8 values layout. Patch planned in runtime core (see PR 4123).
decision_summary: Proceed with hybrid profile as default experimental path due to best latency/quality trade-off in early runs.
Adopt MSE-based calibration for per-head scale tuning plus a lightweight KL check to catch distributional shifts.
Profile granularity: per-model per-seq-bucket, not per-customer in first phase to reduce CI surface area.
